_README: POETRY. The page at website/poetry.html renders this file and nothing else:
the waiting line below while `poems` sits empty, and a chronology rail, a
filter bar and one bay per piece once verse arrives.
NOTHING REACHES THIS FILE BY HAND. 89 pieces sit split and gitignored under
poetry-source/, each awaiting a metadata block the owner fills in through the
local tool. Only would_publish: yes crosses over, and only the fields in
scripts/poetry-curate.py -> PUBLIC travel with it. Write it with:
python scripts/poetry-curate.py --publish
Read projects/poetry/README.md before touching any of it, and CLAUDE.md on
why poetry-source/ never enters git: those files hold dated journal entries,
named people and private reflection in the same pages as the verse.
A piece carries: slug, title, text (line breaks survive verbatim — the page
sets white-space: pre-line), written, written_precision, year, era, lines,
length_band, season, time_of_day, age, mood, disposition, what_i_was_reading,
theme (a list), form. Never written_for, occasion, redactions_needed, notes
or kind — those stay in poetry-source/ whatever anybody types anywhere.
`facets` below holds a copy of projects/poetry/taxonomy.json, so the page
labels its filters off the same list the curation tool draws its chips from.
Edit the taxonomy, not this copy; --publish refreshes it.
waiting: The verse waits on its author. He knows where it lives.

_README: THE FACETS. One source of truth for every bucket a reader sorts by, read by
scripts/poetry-index.py (which writes the vocabulary into each poem's
metadata block as a comment), by scripts/poetry-curate.py (which draws the
chips in the local curation tool), and copied into website/data/poetry.json
so the page labels its own filters without a second list to keep in step.
PUBLIC BY DESIGN. Every field here reaches the web. The private fields —
written_for, occasion, redactions_needed, mood, disposition, notes — live in
the poem files only and never enter this taxonomy. projects/poetry/README.md
carries the pipeline and the reason the gate stands where it does.
Add a bucket by adding it here. Both scripts and the page pick it up on the
next run; a poem already tagged keeps whatever it holds.
